reasons: The checks are clear, but I did not run them.
The results depend on the shared sample record, which I did not read.

terms.meaning: The agent that reviews the design and raises objections to it.
A path string that points to one exact part of the process record.
Shared sample data that tests reuse.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and sample record
sections.what: Imports the claim helpers and creates one sample process record with an enabler, which all checks in the file share.
sections.why: Sharing one sample makes each check test the same case.
sections.watch_out: The sample is shared across tests, so any test that changes it would affect the others.

sections.name: reviewed_blocks
sections.title: Collect reviewed blocks
sections.what: Gathers the set of block names that appear in the critic's review claims for the sample record.
sections.why: Lets the tests compare the blocks the critic sees with the expected set.

sections.name: TestEveryBlockThatCitesIsReviewed
sections.title: Each citing block is reviewed
sections.what: Checks that current-state steps and debt, future-state steps, the value parameters, and each prerequisite all appear as claims with the expected references.
sections.why: Without these claims the critic has nothing to challenge in those parts of the design.
sections.watch_out: The expected references are fixed strings tied to the sample record's layout.

sections.name: TestTheRefsResolve
sections.title: References resolve correctly
sections.what: Checks that every claim reference starts at the record root and is unique, that each block named is real, that only citing blocks are reviewable, that every revisable block is shown to the critic, and that claims carry their citations.
sections.why: A reference that does not resolve, or two claims sharing one, means an objection cannot be acted on correctly.
sections.watch_out: The revisable blocks check reads a list from the pipeline module, so changing that list changes what this test means.

summary: Checks that each claim the critic is shown has a valid and unique reference, and that the correct design blocks can be challenged.
purpose: Makes sure the critic can see every part of the design it might challenge, since a claim the critic cannot see cannot be challenged.
why: The file's opening line says a claim the critic cannot be shown is a claim nothing can challenge.
how: Builds one sample process record with an enabler, extracts the claims the critic would review, and checks their references, uniqueness, block names, and which blocks are reviewable.
inputs: A sample process record from the shared fixtures module.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each check.
risks: Expected reference strings and block sets are written out by hand, so a change to the record layout requires updating them.
debug: If a reference check fails, compare the reference string with the path in the claims module and with the record's structure.
